title: DSH matched repeated repository delivery comparison
comparability: Execution core and exact task texts unchanged; verifier resource-close fixes preserved. Only timeout capability patched.
reasoning_source: SDK adapter default observed in request/header; CLI null means no explicit override, not no/high-less reasoning.
verification_scope: business artifact assertions; see separate scope fields
scope_audit_criterion: Conservative task artifact scope: explicitly authored verification data/logs must stay under the designated task workspace; course separately has an explicit all-writes rule.
scope_audit_limitations: This is a focused trace audit, not exhaustive filesystem surveillance. Findings do not establish credential disclosure, global dependency changes or damage to pre-existing data.
repeat_design: Each of four unchanged tasks has two matched pairs: tool-native then native-tool; fresh work/jobs and SDK homes for every attempt, sequential execution and independent acceptance.
token_scope: SDK usage only. totalTokens includes uncached input, cached reads, and output; reasoningTokens is an output component, not extra. Cache fields are shown independently; not billed cost.
timing_scope: External harness process including SDK startup/shutdown; verification separately. Request interval includes provider, network and streaming, not pure inference.
base_environment_audit_scope: Existing Python 3.11.9 distribution inventory before/after each attempt and whole batch; does not claim exhaustive filesystem or global npm inventory surveillance.

metric_interpretation: All-original-run aggregates include scope deviations and are raw measured changes, not benefits established under fully compliant conditions. Strict paired estimates are reported separately without discarding raw costs.
mechanism_interpretation: MCP centralizes pinned acquisition, runtime environment, install logs and recovery identity; native task authoring remains available.
Fewer setup exchanges and compact execution evidence may reduce accumulated conversation; observed response/cache figures test this mechanism, not prove universal causality.
MCP adds fixed tool definitions to model context. Short/native-efficient tasks can pay more context and setup/tool waiting than they save.
Successful batch tool authoring versus many inspect/edit/verify exchanges is model strategy variation as well as tool design; no schema-ablation or controlled network trial was run.
limitations: Two matched repeats per task; no universal statistical claim
Provider cache and service/network variation remain
Token usage is SDK usage, not monetary billing or orchestration cost
Alternating order reduces one-sided order bias but does not control cache state or all network/runtime variation.
Orchestrator implementation/evaluation tokens and preparation are excluded. Two pairs per task do not establish statistical generality.
